_comment: Hand-corrected layouts: classes where the recovered type is demonstrably wrong about a
member's TYPE, with the evidence for each written down beside it. Offsets and sizeof are
never changed here - only how the bytes at a known offset are spelled - and merge_layouts
refuses an entry whose size disagrees with the one already recorded.
This is the narrowest of the layout sources and should stay that way. An inference belongs in
layouts_from_*.json, a recovered type in layouts_kit.json; this file is only for a reading
taken directly out of the binary that contradicts both.

evidence: The IDB type gives dword0/dwordC/gap24[128] - correct offsets, no types - so the fields at
0x18 and 0x1C came out u32 when they hold floats, and everything from 0x24 came out as two
with a2 bounded by `a2 <= 1`. this[a2+6] is 0x18 + 4*a2 and this[a2+4] is 0x10 + 4*a2, so
0x18 is two floats and 0x10 is the two Timers already recorded.
so the region is TWO 132-byte blocks, and 0x24 + 2*132 = 0x12C, the size the binary
allocates. Within a block at base B it writes 4*v9+36 -> B+0x00 (the f32* argument),
4*v9+68 -> B+0x20 (the i32* argument), 4*v9+100 -> B+0x40 (the i32 argument),
128*a2+132+4*v5 -> B+0x60, and increments *((_DWORD *)v6 + 41) -> B+0x80. v5 is a free-slot
index found by scanning B+0x00 and capped at 8, which is what fixes each array at 8 entries.
The constructor at 0x004D56C0 agrees independently: its loop runs 8 times at stride 4 over
the eight bases 0x24, 0x44, 0x64, 0x84, 0xA8, 0xC8, 0xE8 and 0x108, writing -1 to 0x84 and
0x108 - the two SampleState arrays - and 0 to the rest.
Flat per-channel arrays rather than a nested struct only because layouts.json cannot express
one; the offsets are what the still-assembly code actually reads.
